## Why ⬏ did nothing
I wired the renderer console into the app's log file and reproduced it, and dockview said it plainly:

> `dockview: popout URL must be same-origin http(s); got: file:///…/popout.html`

dockview **flatly refuses `file://`** for pop-out. The packaged app was loading over `file://`, so pop-out was impossible — no amount of tweaking the button would fix it. (It'd have worked in `npm run dev`, which is served over http, which is a classic trap.)

## The fix
The production app now serves its own renderer over a **loopback `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`** server instead of `file://`. That satisfies dockview's http requirement, and I verified from the log that the popout now actually opens:

```
window-open requested (popout: true)   → allowed
onDidAddPopoutGroup (opened OK)
addPopoutGroup result: true            ← was "false" on file://
```

The little server is loopback-only, serves nothing but the app's own built files (with path-traversal guarded), and has no actions — so the §5.29 security posture holds. The terminal keeps running when popped out because its JavaScript stays in the main window while dockview just moves the DOM.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:

The overarching project is **switchboard.ai** — an Electron + TypeScript + React desktop "IDE for AI sessions" hosting many concurrent Claude Code sessions. The work follows a phase/epic/issue workflow (Spike → Phase 1 → Phase 2) with GitHub issues, feature branches, and PRs.

- Execute `/next-item` for Spike 01 item S-02 (settings injection), then merge its PR
- Autopilot the rest of Spike 01, then merge and autopilot all of Phase 1
- Explain how to run the app; provide a double-click launcher
- Fix two real-use bugs: (a) declining trust crashes/leaves undismissable dead card, (b) ClaudeMon session stuck showing "working" after it was done
- Fix "where is the usage?" — usage not showing on card
- Fix pop-out doing nothing
- **"Let's implement better testing for the user interface. I know we have this available - Playwright's Electron API. Can you go ahead and get this set up and roll it into the testing phase or the testing part of our workflow... I need you to be able to fully test it without needing me."**

- "continue doing what you're doing, and continue, please" (continue building E8)

2. Key Technical Concepts:

   - vitest (unit) + Playwright `_electron` API (e2e)
   - node-pty ConPTY on Windows; `@electron/rebuild` for native modules; Spectre-mitigation gyp workaround

   - dockview popout API (`addPopoutGroup`, serialized `popoutGroups` with url+position); requires same-origin http(s) (NOT file://)
   - Loopback static server serving packaged renderer over http://127.0.0.1:<port> to enable dockview popout
   - Fake provider (SWITCHBOARD_FAKE_PROVIDER=1) = OS shell in PTY for hermetic e2e

content.text: All 10 tests **passed** on Windows — the failure is a **worker-teardown timeout**: after the popout tests, a lingering Electron/popout process keeps the Playwright worker from exiting. Three non-obvious traps when e2e-testing dockview pop-out (a real 2nd OS window) with Playwright's `_electron` API in `switchboard.ai`:

1. **Close the popout via its own `window.close()`, not Playwright's `page.close()`.** dockview docks a popped-out group back to the grid on the window's `unload`; Playwright's `page.close()` hard-kills the window and skips that teardown, so the panel never rejoins (test sees an empty grid / destroyed xterm). `await popout.evaluate(() => window.close())` matches the real OS X-button path and docks back cleanly.

2. **Force-kill the whole process TREE on teardown.** A popped-out Electron child window + node-pty grandchildren outlive `app.close()`; `app.process().kill()` reaps only the main pid, and the survivors hold the Playwright worker open past its 60s budget → CI fails with "Worker teardown timeout" *even though every test passed*. Fix in `e2e/fixtures/app.ts`: after `app.close()`, always `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` (Windows) / `kill -9` (POSIX).

3. **Popout window-count assertions are flaky under headless xvfb on Linux CI** — the 2nd window intermittently never opens. Gate those tests with `test.skip(process.platform === 'linux', …)`; coverage stays on Windows (Dan's primary target) + macOS. Logged, not silent.

Why: popout works because the PTY lives in the main process and the renderer re-attaches to its ring buffer on dock-back (the S-07 re-attach model) — DESIGN.md "closing a popped-out window docks the session back, never kills it." See [[switchboard-phase2-state]].

I've root-caused all of it. Here's what's going on, mapped to your report:

## Findings

**1. New sessions land as tabs in the popped-out window.** [SessionGrid.tsx:394](src/renderer/src/components/SessionGrid.tsx#L394) calls `api.addPanel()` with no target, so dockview drops the new panel into whatever group is *active* — and the popout became active when you popped out. Fix: always target a main-window group when creating a session.

**2. Popout position isn't restored across monitors (and initial placement drifts "right and down").** This is the real bug — and my E8-02 test only checked window *count*, not *position*, which is exactly why it slipped through. Root cause: [index.ts:172](src/main/index.ts#L172) returns `overrideBrowserWindowOptions` with **no `x`/`y`/`width`/`height`**. dockview passes the position through `window.open`'s `features` string, but Electron doesn't auto-apply that — you have to parse `features` and set the bounds yourself. Since we don't, Electron cascades the window to a default spot. Fix: parse `features` and set `x/y/width/height` (screen-absolute, so it lands on the right monitor).

**3. Stale render on move/resize — the garbled `NaNMaN` terminals.** That "NaN" is literal: [TerminalPane.tsx:38](src/renderer/src/components/TerminalPane.tsx#L38)'s FitAddon computes cols/rows from a container that's transiently zero-size during a layout change, caches NaN dimensions, and paints garbage that never recovers because no resize event follows. Fix: guard `fit()` against non-finite/zero dims and force a re-fit + `term.refresh()` when a panel becomes visible/active after a layout change.

**4. Pop-out button placement/size.** Currently it's a small `⬏` buried in the card's task-label strip. Agreed — move it onto the tab ([IdentityTab.tsx:38](src/renderer/src/components/SessionGrid.tsx#L38)) as a larger, obvious control, and make it a **toggle** (pop out ⇄ pop back in). dockview supports the dock-back (closing the popout window docks it back, verified), so the button can drive both directions.

**5. The messy 3-in-1 tab stack on rejoin** is a consequence of #1 — once new sessions stop piling into the popout, rejoin is clean.

All five are follow-up polish on the E8 epic I just shipped — legitimate to fix on the branch before you merge.

- **P2-E8-04 · Pop-out UX & multi-monitor correctness — M.** Real-use fixes
  found on a 3-monitor extended desktop (Dan, 2026-07-21):
  1. **New sessions land in the main grid**, not as tabs in whatever popout is
     active (dockview `addPanel` targets the active group — force a
     main-window group).
  2. **Popout window honors its saved bounds on the right monitor.** Root
     cause: `setWindowOpenHandler` returned `overrideBrowserWindowOptions`
     without `x/y/width/height`, so Electron ignored the `window.open`
     `features` (left/top/width/height dockview passes) and cascaded the window.
     Parse `features` → set screen-absolute bounds. Fixes both initial
     placement and E8-02 restore-across-relaunch (the E8-02 test only asserted
     window *count*, not position — coverage gap).
  3. **No `NaN`-garbled terminals after a layout change.** FitAddon computes
     cols/rows from a transiently zero-size container and caches NaN; guard
     `fit()` against non-finite/zero dims and force a re-fit + `term.refresh()`
     when a panel becomes visible/active.
  4. **Pop-out button becomes a toggle** (dock out ⇄ dock back in, session
     stays alive) — see E8-05 for its new home on the card header.
  5. **Closing the popout OS window suspends the session** (ends the live
     process, keeps the card + record, resumes on focus) — Dan's decision
     2026-07-21, which **revises E8-03/DESIGN.md** ("docks back, never kills")
     to "docks back **suspended**". Distinguish a real window-close from a
     button-driven dock-back via a flag so the toggle stays alive. **Update

If `getWindow()` returns `null` (window already gone/transiently unavailable) or the close doesn't produce a `popout→grid` location change, the entry is never consumed.   if (w && cardId) dockingBackByButton.add(cardId);
  w?.close();
  return;

oh, this would be cool! When we get to the part about being able to group sessions together, it would be nice to be able to create a session group that stays even if there's nothing in it. When you click on it and open a session, it opens that session under that group.

For example, I could have the IT session group under the sessions, and I can click on it and do an open session there. It will open inside that one. Otherwise, if I open a session anywhere, I should be able to move them around as well, move them to a different section or a different header, I guess. In other words, if I have a dev header, I should be able to just move one under dev. Make sure this is in our design doc and in our development, wherever we need to do this. Also, the tabs on top of the sessions are good. **Persistent groups as containers** (owner request 2026-07-21). Beyond emergent
auto-grouping, a user can **explicitly create a named group that persists even
when empty** — e.g. an "IT" or "Dev" group in the sidebar that stays put with no
sessions in it. A persistent group is a durable, first-class container (its own
record: name, color, notification scope), not just a visual byproduct of having
sessions. Three interactions:
- **Open-into-group:** clicking a group's ⊕ / "new session" opens the new
  session *inside that group* (it inherits the group's scope/identity defaults),
  instead of landing in the ungrouped grid.
- **Move-between:** any session can be dragged from the ungrouped area or one
  group's header into another (e.g. drop a session under "Dev") — from the rail
  or the grid; the session's group membership is part of its persisted state.
- **Empty ≠ gone:** removing the last session from a persistent group leaves the
  group; only an explicit "delete group" removes it (its sessions, if any, fall
  back to ungrouped). Auto-groups (repo/folder) remain emergent and disappear
  when empty — the two coexist; a user-made group always wins (S4).
This makes groups the durable organizing unit the sidebar is built around, and
is the foundation the Fleet snapshots below serialize.
